title_zh: 凌晨兩點的第二位觀眾
story_zh: 「第二位觀眾已加入。」凌晨兩點，手機突然跳出這行字。我沒有開直播。下一行寫著：「共享你的視線中。」我獨居，門窗全鎖。我閉左眼，螢幕立刻黑了一半。有人正在使用我的眼睛。我開前鏡頭。沙發上坐著穿同款睡衣的女人，長髮遮臉。轉頭一看，沙發空無一人。洗手間鏡子裡，倒影慢了半秒才抬頭。她盯著我，一次也沒有眨眼。手機問：「要保留哪位觀眾？」我按下「保留本人」。倒數開始。鏡中的我忽然笑了，指向那道反鎖的房門。我切斷網路，把手機塞進抽屜。抽屜裡傳出我的聲音：「你怎麼知道，按鈕上的本人是你？」房門自己打開。手機亮起：「第一位觀眾已離線。」鏡中的女人走出來，拿起手機，輕輕關燈。我想叫，卻只能看見她的手指隔著玻璃滑動。原來被關在螢幕裡的，從來不是那個觀眾。通知最後寫著：「視線已歸還原主人。」
story_en: SECOND VIEWER JOINED. At two in the morning, my phone flashed that warning. I wasn’t streaming. Below it appeared: SHARING YOUR VISION. I lived alone. Every door was locked. When I closed my left eye, half the screen went dark. Someone wasn’t watching my phone. They were looking through me. I opened the front camera. A woman in my pajamas sat on the sofa, her hair covering her face. I turned. The sofa was empty. In the bathroom mirror, my reflection raised her head half a second late. She stared without blinking. My phone asked: WHICH VIEWER SHOULD REMAIN? I tapped KEEP ME. A countdown began. My reflection smiled and pointed at the bedroom door, locked from the inside. I disconnected the Wi-Fi and hid the phone in a drawer. My own voice whispered from it: HOW DO YOU KNOW THE WORD ME MEANS YOU? The bedroom door opened. The screen announced: FIRST VIEWER DISCONNECTED. The woman stepped out of the mirror, picked up my phone, and turned off the light. I tried to scream. All I could see was her finger swiping across glass. I was inside the screen. The final message said: VISION RETURNED TO ITS ORIGINAL OWNER.
